game.setlist.deterministic: Three seeded directives selected from six authored contracts.
game.setlist.server-authoritative: Progress, timeout, reward, and result state are owned by the local Node host.
game.show-memory.server-authoritative: Bounded night history, total score, best result, cleared acts, round seed, and next-Setlist preview are owned by the runtime host; aborting a round does not consume it.

game.conductor.receipt-adaptive: The host deterministically selects OPENING, RECONNECT, LOCK-IN, or HEADLINER plans from the latest bounded authoritative receipt; adapted act kinds are fixed before the next round starts.
game.conductor.transparent: Every plan carries a stable mode, title, short cue, source round, full reason, and exact act kinds; no difficulty or objective change is hidden from the room.
state.conductor.schema-migration: Restored pre-cue checkpoints are normalized into the current Conductor contract without losing result state, show history, the completed-round receipt, or the next adapted plan.
ui.conductor.cross-surface: The shared lobby/result and 390x844 controller expose the same RECONNECT SET reason, cue, Round 2 identity, and CALL & RESPONSE / PASS THE MIC / CHAIN REACTION plan.
input.ai.idle-noop: Support AI idle decisions outside active play no longer advance action sequences or fill the bounded input ledger with rejected synthetic actions.
test.conductor: Core, HTTP, recovery, and handback tests cover deterministic plan modes, exact adapted act kinds, cross-process persistence, legacy-state migration, receipt transport, and idle-AI no-op behavior.
visual.conductor.journey: A full managed opening round produced a receipt-driven RECONNECT SET; shared result/lobby and portrait result/active states visibly exposed its reason and exact plan with measured no-overflow fit.

game.room-signal.human-authority: Only current human players may cast or replace a next-round signal vote; a live AI attempt returned HTTP 403 without changing revision, votes, or plan.
game.room-signal.deterministic-resolutio: The server counts one replaceable vote per eligible human, resolves ties with the stable TOGETHER / BOLD / FLOW order, and maps the winner to one exact authored three-act plan.
state.room-signal.round-bound: The bounded schema targets exactly the next unplayed round, survives fresh-process checkpoint recovery, is copied into the consumed Conductor receipt, and rolls forward only after round completion.
ui.room-signal.cross-surface: The 390x844 human controller exposes three accessible vote buttons and current tally; the 1280x720 shared lobby exposes the winning signal, vote count, transparent reason, and exact next plan. AI controllers do not receive voting authority.
test.room-signal: Core, HTTP, and fresh-process recovery tests cover authorization, validation, idempotence, vote replacement, deterministic ties, exact plan application, round consumption, receipt storage, and checkpoint persistence.
visual.room-signal.journey: In managed session session-1785246383789, Mike selected BOLD on the portrait controller; shared lobby and both active surfaces visibly rendered the exact HUMAN SPOTLIGHT / PASS THE MIC / RIDE THE STATIC plan with zero measured overflow and zero console warnings/errors.

game.human-agency.gated: Every set contains a human-required act; support AI cannot clear the full setlist alone.

ui.shared-screen.setlist: Managed browser verification passed at 1280x720 in lobby, active play, results, replay, and reset recovery.
ui.controller.setlist: Managed portrait-browser verification passed at 390x844 with the directive and all touch controls visible without overflow.
ui.show-memory.cross-surface: Shared lobby, active directive, receipt, replay, reset recovery, and portrait controller expose the same authoritative show/round identity and next plan.
ui.recovery.cross-surface: The shared display exposes RECONNECTING then HOST RESTORED, while seat observation gives controllers an explicit REJOINED cue; both return to the same authoritative show identity.

state.checkpoint.atomic: The local host writes a size-limited schema envelope through same-directory temporary write, fsync, and atomic rename; checkpoints are roster-bound and expire after 30 minutes by default.
state.session.restore: A same-host, same-roster runtime relaunch restores lobby, countdown, active, or result state; live deadlines are rebased so downtime does not consume the round. This is not host migration.
input.sequence.restart-safe: Accepted sequence counters survive restart, stale sequences remain rejected, and held movement/pulse buffers restore neutral to prevent duplicated or stuck input.

game.handback.authoritative: A completed-show summary is projected only from server-owned Show Memory and includes the bounded last round, next plan, totals, best result, and cleared acts.
transport.hub-result.callback: Managed runtimes can POST a capped result envelope only to the configured loopback Game Hub /game/end route; sender, receiver, stored result, Hub lobby state, and stopped child were observed for one managed session.
state.handback.clean-relaunch: A successful explicit handback retires the show checkpoint before Game Hub ends the child; the next managed launch was a fresh lobby with zero history and totals. Callback failure re-enables checkpoint persistence.
ui.shared-screen.handback: After at least one completed round, the shared display exposes a two-step Return to Game Hub action and a visible SHOW SAVED transition; the action is hidden for a fresh show.

test.setlist.rules: Determinism, rotation, human gating, reward, and result closure are covered.
test.setlist.http: HTTP state and seat observation expose the authoritative setlist.
test.show-memory.replay: Core and HTTP tests prove deterministic seed advancement, changed directives, bounded history, persistent totals, and abort-safe replay identity.
test.recovery.fresh-process: A separate-process HTTP test proves restore with paused time, neutral input, sequence continuity, explicit New Show reset, and safe fallbacks for corrupt, expired, and roster-mismatched checkpoints.
test.hub-handback: A fake loopback receiver plus runtime HTTP test proves availability/refusal rules, exact receiver payload, single-send behavior, checkpoint retirement, and fresh relaunch.
visual.setlist.journey: One complete managed round visibly rotated all three acts, cleared one act, awarded 240 bonus points, rendered a 1/3 receipt, replayed into countdown, and recovered to a clean lobby.
visual.show-memory.replay: Managed Round 1 at seed 12026 visibly previewed and replayed into the exact changed Round 2 at seed 12027 on desktop and portrait surfaces; reset preserved history and the unconsumed Round 2 plan.
visual.recovery.managed-restart: A managed Game Hub stop/start visibly traversed RECONNECTING to HOST RESTORED and recovered the exact active round identity, score, revision, clock, player position, Setlist act, and input sequence; controller observation rendered REJOINED.
visual.handback-control: The managed lobby visibly exposed Return to Game Hub, a non-destructive confirmation state, and SHOW SAVED · RETURNING before the callback stopped the runtime.

judgment.human.game-night: Requires Mike and representative real groups.

visual.physical-phone: No physical phone is connected to this task.

visual.hub-home-navigation: The in-app verifier blocks direct rendering of local port 8790, so the final browser landing on Game Hub is not visually observed even though Hub state and stored-result application passed.

network.production-scale: This build is intentionally local-only and has no production matchmaking substrate.
